# Closure and Escalation Notes

**Rundll32 Proxy Execution From Suspicious Context** · `T1218.011_rundll32_suspicious_execution` · [T1218.011](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/011/)

Fill in only what you checked. A confirmed attack is never closed from the queue: send the escalation note instead.

## Benign Positive

The rule fired on real activity that is expected and authorized.

```text
Alert:        T1218.011_rundll32_suspicious_execution for <host> at <time, UTC>
Observed:     Image=<value>  OriginalFileName=<value>  CommandLine=<value>
Checked:      1. Retrieve the referenced DLL, hash it, and check its signer -> <result>
              2. Check the parent process -> <result>
              3. For no-argument rundll32, look for network connections from the PID -> <result>
Benign:       <which known source below> - confirmed by <change record, owner or ticket>
Disposition:  Benign Positive
Tuning:       none | msi_custom_actions (proposed)
```

Known benign sources for this detection:
- Installers whose custom actions load DLLs from %TEMP%

Never tune:
- Never filter javascript:, vbscript:, RunHTMLApplication or comsvcs: they have no common legitimate use with rundll32.

Escalate when any of these holds:
1. DLL is unsigned or new to the environment
2. javascript:, vbscript: or comsvcs MiniDump present
3. rundll32 with no arguments that makes network connections

Risk conditions: suspicious parent +20 · payload in user writable path +10 · host is critical +15 · known vendor software -25.

Containment options, after the evidence above is preserved:
1. Quarantine the DLL
2. Isolate the host if code executed
3. Block any contacted infrastructure
